questions.q: A column uses 25 mm longitudinal bars and 10 mm ties. If the other spacing limit is a 450 mm least dimension, which spacing limit controls?
questions.ref: BLDGTECH - JOE PREBOARD, source items 9–13 (reworded situation and questions)
questions.n: The three limits are 16×25 = 400 mm, 48×10 = 480 mm, and 450 mm. The smallest is 400 mm.

questions.q: What joint results when one concrete placement has already hardened before fresh concrete is placed against it?
questions.n: The source defines this condition as a cold joint.

questions.q: What reinforced-concrete floor system consists of a slab supported by reinforced-concrete beams, often cast monolithically?
questions.n: The source defines the beam-and-slab floor as a slab carried by reinforced-concrete beams, commonly cast as one system.

questions.q: What is the continuous wire support used to hold reinforcing bars near the bottom of a slab?
questions.n: The source identifies a bolster as the continuous wire bar support used beneath slab reinforcement.

questions.q: If every tie is wired to all eight longitudinal bars using 0.40 m of wire per intersection, how many metres of tie wire are required?
questions.ref: BLDGTECH - JOE PREBOARD, source items 9–13 (reworded situation and questions)
questions.n: The 598 ties create 598×8 intersections; multiplying by 0.40 m gives 1,913.6 m of tie wire.

questions.q: With 40 mm cover on each side, what tie-side dimension should be used for A and B?
questions.ref: BLDGTECH - JOE PREBOARD, source items 9–13 (reworded situation and questions)
questions.n: The tie side is the 500 mm column dimension less 40 mm cover at both faces: 500 − 80 = 420 mm.

questions.q: A 400 mm square column has 40 mm cover. Ignoring bar-center adjustments and following the source's tie-side method, what side dimension is used for the closed tie?
questions.ref: BLDGTECH - JOE PREBOARD, source items 9–13 (reworded situation and questions)
questions.n: Using the source's simplified method, subtract cover from both faces: 400 − 2×40 = 320 mm.

questions.q: What is the term for removing formwork after concrete has cured sufficiently?
questions.n: The source uses 'stripping' for removing forms from cured concrete.

questions.q: What composite material is made from cement mortar reinforced with several closely spaced layers of steel wire mesh?
questions.n: The source defines ferrocement as mortar reinforced with multiple closely spaced layers of wire mesh.

questions.q: What term describes transverse reinforcement such as ties, hoops, and spirals in columns?
questions.n: The source defines ties, hoops, and spirals in column-like members as lateral reinforcement.

questions.q: Using 53 m of tie wire per kilogram, what mass of tie wire is required for all 26 columns?
questions.ref: BLDGTECH - JOE PREBOARD, source items 9–13 (reworded situation and questions)
questions.n: 1,913.6 m ÷ 53 m/kg is about 36.1 kg; the source's matching whole-kilogram choice is 37 kg.

questions.q: Using L = 2(A+B)+20d, what is the cutting length of one 10 mm closed tie?
questions.ref: BLDGTECH - JOE PREBOARD, source items 9–13 (reworded situation and questions)
questions.n: With A = B = 0.42 m and d = 0.01 m, the computed tie length is 1.88 m.

questions.q: A square tie has A = B = 0.32 m and uses a 10 mm bar. Using L = 2(A+B)+20d, what cutting length is obtained?
questions.ref: BLDGTECH - JOE PREBOARD, source items 9–13 (reworded situation and questions)

questions.q: What defect consists of voids where mortar failed to fill spaces around coarse aggregate?
questions.n: The source defines honeycomb as voided concrete caused by inadequate mortar filling around coarse aggregate.

questions.q: What term describes concrete with a relatively high cement content?
questions.n: The source identifies high-cement-content concrete as rich concrete.

questions.q: In a rectangular flat slab, what reinforcement pattern uses bands parallel to both adjacent edges and both diagonals?
questions.n: The source defines four-way reinforcement as bands running along the two principal directions and both diagonals.

questions.q: Which concrete admixture acts as distributed micro-reinforcement and is commonly used to limit plastic-shrinkage cracking in slabs?
questions.n: The source identifies fibers as micro-reinforcing material used to reduce plastic-shrinkage cracking; GFRC also relies on fibers.

questions.q: For all 26 columns, what is the theoretical total length of 10 mm tie bar before commercial-length rounding?
questions.ref: BLDGTECH - JOE PREBOARD, source items 9–13 (reworded situation and questions)
questions.n: There are 26×23 = 598 ties. At 1.88 m per tie, the total is 1,124.24 m.

questions.q: What maximum tie spacing is controlled by the governing limit for these columns?
questions.ref: BLDGTECH - JOE PREBOARD, source items 9–13 (reworded situation and questions)
questions.n: The three limits are 16×20 = 320 mm, 48×10 = 480 mm, and 500 mm. The smallest value governs.

questions.q: What weak cementitious surface layer forms when fines are carried upward by bleeding or separate from the mix?
questions.n: The source describes laitance as a weak layer of cementitious material and fines deposited at surfaces or cavities.

questions.q: Which concrete characteristic is most directly controlled by the water-cement ratio in the source question?
questions.n: The source associates water-cement ratio with concrete strength.

questions.q: For best crack-control effectiveness in a slab-on-grade, where should temperature and shrinkage reinforcement be located?
o: Anywhere in the slab with equal effect
Within the upper third of the slab thickness
questions.n: The source places temperature and shrinkage reinforcement in the upper third for maximum effectiveness.

questions.q: Which reinforced-concrete cladding material is specifically associated with fiber reinforcement in the source?
questions.n: The source explicitly connects glass-fiber-reinforced concrete (GFRC) cladding panels with fibrous admixtures.

questions.q: Using 6.0 m commercial bars, what whole-number order quantity is closest to the required 10 mm tie-bar stock?
questions.ref: BLDGTECH - JOE PREBOARD, source items 9–13 (reworded situation and questions)
questions.n: The theoretical requirement is about 1,124 m. Dividing by 6 m gives about 187.4 bars, so the matching source choice is 200 bars.

questions.q: Using the governing spacing, approximately how many closed ties are required along one 7.00 m column?
questions.ref: BLDGTECH - JOE PREBOARD, source items 9–13 (reworded situation and questions)
questions.n: Seven metres divided by 0.32 m gives 21.875 spaces. Rounding up the number of spaces and providing a tie at the end gives 23 ties.
